event.summary: Retiring tmux intentionally ends running legacy terminals
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 1ed482dde220452e424973faf38a5e1318986333. TLDR: Updating a host to this release ends any agents and terminal tabs still running in the old terminal system and loses their live terminal contents; they do not survive the supervisor upgrade. Details: This is the potentially-highest consequence considered while reviewing removal of the sink and its driver. core.rs:6147-6151 calls OldTerminals::end_private_server before reload; core/old_terminals.rs:168-172 calls end_server, and core.rs:6675-6679 deliberately resolves every legacy tmux row to no terminal. This departs from the ordinary sessions-outlive-supervisor contract but is explicitly specified. Exact SPEC.md, Terminal experience, lines 3003-3011: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' (The source uses an ASCII apostrophe in host's.) The same paragraph says a still-live old agent becomes interrupted, an already-ended one keeps its outcome but loses its last screen, and old tabs are closed. Exact SPEC.md, Durability and resume, lines 3470-3473: 'only a host reboot takes sessions down (and, once, the update that ended old terminals; see Terminal experience).' SPEC_impl.md, Terminal substrate: private tmux server, lines 2882-2930, fully specifies this transition, cleanup residuals and continued startup on failure. Suggested bucket: highest/loss of user-owned processes and live terminal work, if treated as a defect. Confidence: confirmed intended source behavior; no execution observed. proposed_drop: exact specification exception above explicitly authorizes ending the legacy tmux terminals and discarding their contents during this upgrade. This must receive the caller's independent highest-bucket drop check; it is not an independently established defect. possible_cover: SPEC.md and SPEC_impl.md retirement contract only; other coverage sources were not read. Could-be-highest: true. Scope caveat: this record concerns the authorized removal itself, not an assertion that all adjacent migration cleanup is correct.

TLDR (original wording preserved): Updating a host to this release ends any agents and terminal tabs still running in the old terminal system and loses their live terminal contents; they do not survive the supervisor upgrade. Details: This potentially-highest consequence was considered while reviewing sink/driver removal. core.rs:6147-6151 calls OldTerminals::end_private_server before reload; core/old_terminals.rs:168-172 calls end_server; core.rs:6675-6679 deliberately resolves every old tmux row to no terminal. Synthesis checked conversion :6805-6825 and sweep/commit/notice ordering :7036-7094: legacy live launches are proposed as TerminalEnded, sweeping precedes transition commit, and the ended notice follows a committed interrupted outcome. Exact SPEC.md, Terminal experience, :3006-3008: 'This release ends them: the first time a host's supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' Its paragraph explicitly discards an ended agent's last screen and closes old tabs. Exact SPEC.md, Durability and resume, :3471-3473: 'only a host reboot takes sessions down (and, once, the update that ended old terminals; see Terminal experience).' Known related residual, now made explicit under this same provenance: failed legacy termination can leave a still-running old agent and allow Restart to start a duplicate. Exact acceptance in SPEC.md :3014-3016: 'A failure to end the server or to stop what ran there is logged and never stops the supervisor from starting; those sessions are treated as ended all the same, accepting that a Restart could then start a second agent beside one still running.' SPEC_impl.md Terminal substrate :2880-2991 specifies both the retirement and this residual. This is not new discovery in synthesis. Suggested bucket: highest/loss of user-owned processes, live screens/history and potentially concurrent agents, if treated as a defect. Confidence: confirmed intended source behavior; no execution observed. proposed_drop: only the exact deliberate-retirement and duplicate-on-failed-termination consequences above are accepted by those specification exceptions. This remains a proposal, requiring the caller's independent highest-bucket check; no drop is accepted yet. possible_cover: cited SPEC.md/SPEC_impl.md retirement contract only; excluded coverage sources not read. Could-be-highest: true. Material caveat: that acceptance does not settle misleading update-survival advice, absence of required warning, wrong-target termination, or falsely successful Delete. No concrete distinct route to those consequences was supplied by these assigned deletion patches or established in the checked retained host responsibilities; no comprehensive correctness claim is made for adjacent migration/provisioning/UI implementations.

TLDR: Considered whether retiring tmux-specific tests leaves a surviving terminal action able to act on another session's work, or prompts/excerpts able to use stale terminal identity. A wrong-target close or Delete could end user-owned processes; a prompt sent to the wrong terminal could act on unintended work.
